description: The arm's-length case for one related-party transaction, written down before anybody asks for it. A payment to the manager's own trucking LLC is not wrong; a payment to the manager's own trucking LLC that nobody can price against the market is what a related-party finding actually is. This record holds the price, the reference the price was tested against, and the sentence explaining why the two agree — which is the whole of what IRC §482 and the disclosure schedules ask an operation to have kept.

fields.description: Which entity's transaction this documents. Required — an arm's-length case belongs to the books it defends.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: The counterparty, as a row in the related-party register rather than as free text. A Link and not a Data field on purpose: this is what lets a transaction found in the ledger be matched to its documentation without anybody spelling a name the same way twice.
fields.label: Related Party

fields.description: What kind of dealing this is. A CLOSED LIST because it is what a transaction is matched on — two spellings of 'Management Fee' would let one documented arrangement look undocumented and the finding would be raised against a farm that had done the work.
fields.label: Transaction Type
fields.options:
Purchase of Goods
Sale of Goods
Services Received
Services Provided
Lease — Land
Lease — Equipment
Lease — Housing
Loan Received
Loan Made
Management Fee
Cost Sharing
Guarantee
Other

fields.description: First day this documentation covers. A transfer pricing case is made for a PERIOD rather than for a single invoice — one memo covering a season of hauling is how the work is actually done, and requiring one per invoice is how a control gets abandoned.
fields.label: Period Start

fields.description: Last day this documentation covers, inclusive.
fields.label: Period End

fields.description: DRAFT DOES NOT COVER A TRANSACTION, and the distinction is the point of the field. A started-but-unfinished memo is a different finding from no memo at all, and the control says which — 'the documentation exists and is unfinished' is a morning's work, 'nothing was ever written' is a season's.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The later memo that replaces this one. Set when a period is re-documented — nothing is deleted, because the transactions the old memo defended are still in the ledger and a prior year's schedule still needs the case as it stood.
fields.label: Superseded By

fields.description: What the arrangement is worth over the period covered. The control compares the transactions it finds against this: a memo written for $12,000 of hauling does not document $140,000 of it, and saying so is the difference between documentation and paperwork.
fields.label: Documented Amount

fields.description: How the price was tested. The names are the recognised methods under IRC §482 and the OECD guidelines, so a memo written here uses the vocabulary the examiner already reads in.
fields.label: Pricing Method
fields.options:
Comparable Uncontrolled Price
Resale Price
Cost Plus
Comparable Profits / TNMM
Profit Split
Other

fields.description: WHAT THE PRICE WAS TESTED AGAINST, specifically enough that somebody else could look it up: 'three quotes from independent haulers, Yakima, March 2026', 'USDA custom rates survey, Pacific Northwest, 2025', 'the rate we charge the two unrelated growers on the same route'. Required, because a justification with no reference behind it is an opinion.
fields.label: Market Rate Reference

fields.description: Why this price is the price an unrelated party would have paid. Written for somebody who was not there — an examiner, a lender, an auditor three years later — and the one field on this record that nothing can compute.
fields.label: Arm's-Length Justification

fields.description: The comparable arrangements relied on, one per line, with their prices.
fields.label: Comparables

fields.description: The signed agreement, the quote file, the rate survey — whatever is on the site already. Quotes and surveys that are not can be attached to this record.
fields.label: Supporting Document

fields.description: Who checked it. A memo the preparer also reviewed is not reviewed, and the related-party disclosure report reports that separately rather than counting it as done.
fields.label: Reviewed By

name: Transfer Pricing Documentation
